audit_findings.title: Run-rate acquisition interest is absent from the owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: H1 2026 interest expense was $33.4 million versus $8.8 million in H1 2025: a filed/computed increase of $24.6 million, or $49.2 million annualized before tax
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity-level OE method retains interest expense and does not deduct debt principal, so the post-acquisition interest charge must reduce the OE anchor and every projected cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: On December 29, 2025, the Company borrowed $ 900 million under the Term Facility and an additional $ 250 million under the Revolving Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error, not merely a possibility. The $1.15 billion borrowed immediately before closing generated a substantial recurring charge that is almost absent from 2022-2025 OE. The annualized pre-tax increase equals 16.6% of the $295.7 million anchor, a scale capable of materially lowering intrinsic value even though it would reinforce the existing conclusion that the shares exceed modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE using H1 2026 interest expense, average debt balances, applicable SOFR margins, commitment fees and the 23.5% H1 effective tax rate; then rerun all scenarios without separately deducting debt principal.

audit_findings.title: The operating numerator and current equity claim use different business perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: The acquisitions cost $1,355.4 million in cash and contributed $216.6 million of H1 2026 sales; management reported a negative $4.3 million H1 acquisition impact on operating profit, while Druck, Panametrics and Reuter-Stokes separately contributed $202.1 million of sales and a $3.0 million operating loss
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE anchor excludes acquired operations, while the shares, cash balance, debt, working capital and other bridge inputs represent the post-close consolidated company.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 1, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of Druck, Panametrics and Reuter-Stokes.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated. The omitted perimeter can raise value through acquired earnings and synergies but lower it through interest, amortization-related normalization questions, integration costs, working capital and capital expenditures. The $1.3554 billion purchase outlay is 30.1% of the $4.505 billion base equity value, so the mismatch is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation, even though the filed first-half operating contribution does not establish its normalized value.
audit_findings.action: Construct post-close consolidated OE from the 2026 statements, separating acquisition-related amortization, transaction costs, tariff refunds and working-capital movements; reconcile acquired earnings, financing and reinvestment on one perimeter and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Serial transaction costs may have been treated as nonrecurring
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed pre-tax transaction expenses were $14.8 million in 2025, $8.4 million in 2024 and $39.3 million in 2023, with the 2023 amount related to the separation
audit_findings.mechanism: Any addback raises historical OE and its trend anchor; omitting a normalized recurring acquisition cost also raises forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we recorded pre-tax transaction related expenses of $14.8 million primarily related to the Druck, Panametrics, Reuter-Stokes and Optek acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The costs are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the OE calculations added them back. The 2025 amount alone equals 5.0% of the $295.7 million anchor, but the sustainable acquisition-related portion cannot be inferred because the large 2023 charge concerned the separation. Materiality therefore remains unresolved rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Produce the 2022-2025 OE adjustment ledger, identify every transaction or integration-cost addback, distinguish the separation from recurring acquisition activity, and rerun with a filed-history normalized annual acquisition cost if acquisitions remain part of forecast growth.

audit_findings.title: Environmental indemnities have an unquantified tail beyond recorded accruals
audit_findings.magnitude: Post-2027 exposure is unquantified; the June 30, 2026 filed Goodyear liability was $11.2 million gross less a $1.9 million government-reimbursement receivable, or $9.3 million net
audit_findings.mechanism: Unreserved remediation and indemnity cash payments reduce future OE or require a separate liability deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: It is not possible at this point to reasonably estimate the amount of any obligation in excess of our current accruals through the 2027 forecast period because of the aforementioned uncertainties, in particular, the continued significant changes in the Goodyear Site conditions and additional expectations of remediation activities experienced in recent years.
audit_findings.explanation: The existing net recorded amount is only 0.21% of the $4.505 billion base equity value and is not material by itself. It does not bound the tail: the company states that obligations beyond the current forecast cannot be reasonably estimated, and Crane retains indemnity exposure for Goodyear, Roseland and Crab Orchard. This is an existing unresolved exposure, but the record cannot establish whether its unrecorded amount is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2027 performance-monitoring report, EPA and NJDEP responses, updated consultant cost ranges, GD-OTS allocation information, Redco indemnity terms and available insurance or government recoveries; deduct the probability-weighted post-2027 cash outflows or rerun a disclosed range.

audit_findings.title: Hurricane insurance proceeds may contaminate normalized OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed lost-profit proceeds were $9.3 million; assuming the entire pre-tax amount entered 2025 OE dollar-for-dollar, removing it lowers the computed log-trend anchor by approximately $6.2 million and base value by approximately $1.46 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring 2025 gain can raise the four-year log-trend OE anchor and proportionally raise operating PV, equity value and the buy-below price.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, we also received insurance proceeds for lost profits of $9.3 million, included in Miscellaneous income, net in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: In the conservative full-inclusion sensitivity, the anchor falls about 2.1%, base value falls from $75.72 to approximately $74.26 per share, and the buy-below level falls by about $1.02. That is small relative to the $128.97 gap between the $204.69 market price and the $75.72 base value, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion. The actual effect could be smaller because the proceeds were pre-tax and may replace genuinely lost operating profit.
audit_findings.action: Trace miscellaneous income through the 2025 OE worksheet and document whether the $9.3 million was retained, removed or matched against demonstrably lost operating profit; correct the normalization if necessary, without treating it as a conclusion-changing issue.
